utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. I'm sorry we were a little delayed coming in. Could the witness be brought in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. If I could remind you of the affirmation you took at the commencement of your evidence, it still applies. Yes, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Jokic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask the usher for his assistance and show the witness Exhibit 500 from tab 2. Exhibit 500 from tab 2.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: There is no Exhibit 500.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P100.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, you said that this schematic represents the structure for the 2nd Operations Group, and the date of it is the 6th of December, 1991. And this is the organigramme of the 9th Military Naval Sector. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, objection. It's of the 2OG on the top of the organigramme.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Is that the organigramme of the 2nd Operational Group on the 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In that organigramme, can we see the units which were subordinated to the 9th Military Naval Sector?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: On that same day?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You also said that the 472nd Motorised Brigade at that time was within the composition of the 2nd Corps. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. On the 6th of November it was to have been pulled out. That was what the order was. But due to force of circumstance --

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I'm just asking you about the 6th of December now.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the 6th of December it was within the composition of the 2nd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You said that the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade was attached to the 9th Military Naval Sector to effect the blockade from the south and south-east direction or axis from the Trebinje area. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not what I said. I didn't ask to have that battalion attached to make up a full complement. I had one single unit of men, and that was a mixed detachment. And that was on the 6th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Apart from the units that are set out in this organigramme, which other units came within the composition of the 9th Military Naval Sector on the 6th of December, 1991? Could you tell us that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could I ask the usher's assistance to hand this piece of paper to the witness so that he can show us the formation of the 9th VPS or Military Naval Sector. Could the usher hand this piece of paper to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, may the Prosecution simply inquire what is the purpose of the exercise when the units are also shown on the organigramme of the 2nd Operational Group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That will be a question Mr. Rodic will inform us about shortly, I hope.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The purpose of it is, Your Honour, that this organigramme doesn't show the complete 9th VPS with all its units. Here we have only five units that are shown within the composition of the VPS, whereas there were more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And it's important that we know each one of them, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, Your Honour. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you place that piece of paper on --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you place the piece of paper you've just been writing on on the ELMO, please. I should like to ask you to read them out one by one, the units within that composition.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I just be allowed to explain why these units were not listed in my previous organigramme, the one that I compiled for the investigators, and it is this: At the time I understood it that I was asked for infantry units working on land, and that is why at the bottom of the organigramme I listed these ground forces and their units. However, I now see that you are asking for all the units within the composition of the 9th VPS, Military Naval Sector. So can we take it in order?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Yes, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the battery of coast-to-sea missiles, this first one here on the left. Then we come to the next one which is the 9th Mixed Detachment of landing vessels.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next one is the 107th Coastal Group, artillery group, which had stationary batteries that were entrenched in tunnels. That is the coastal unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: May I just interrupt you for a moment. It says 107 OAG. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Now, why in the orders do we find 107 OAD? Is this a divizion or artillery battalion?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is OAG, whereas this 140, the next box, the next unit, is the 140th Mobile Coastal Artillery Battalion, with two mobile batteries. And last time we said and explained that a battery had 130-millimetre weapons, guns, and that the second battery has 85-millimetre guns. So this wasn't challenged at all on every map. We have the five positions indicated of these particular batteries. Now, the next box is the 69th Naval Technical Missile Base, rocket base. And then we come to the 367th Naval Rear Base, logistics base. And next is the 16th Border Naval Detachment, which had four patrol vessels. And the last one, the divizion or artillery battalion, anti-aircraft unit with batteries of 20 and 40 millimetres for the defence -- for air defence. Of course there were other units as well, but they are not significant in this matter, the one we're discussing. If need be, I should be happy to add them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please move the piece of paper so we can see it, see the whole of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And what did you say this last box was?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the divizion or artillery battalion anti-aircraft of 20 and 40 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Are we missing the TOS -- TOC, the technical experimental centre?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But it is not a division within the formation of the 9th VPS. I said earlier on that it was a unit which was subordinated to the military technical institute, which was directly under the supervision of the General Staff. And it was -- here we just had a training centre of the technical experimental centre, the TOC centre, and it was located at Prevlaka. And since at the beginning of combat on the 1st of October, this training centre was subordinated to the commander of the 9th VPS, I inherited that state of affairs when I arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me, please, whether in the exhibits that were tendered here, including your orders of the 10th of November, for example, that mention is made of combat orders and the TOC is also mentioned as well as the order for action for the pieces and weapons. And I'd like to ask you to indicate that regardless of whether it was attached to you temporarily, so that we have this complete organigramme and all the units and compositions, regardless of whether they were temporary ones, or permanently attached and subordinated to you.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, within the frameworks of that technical experimental centre, the TOC, and the training ground - I said this last time, I believe - they had three weapons, three pieces of weaponry for experimental purposes and testing. It was not a combat unit. I'd like to make that clear straight away. And its intention was absolutely not to be deployed for defence purposes. They were three different weapons of three different calibres. And it was clear to one and all that they could not be used and deployed for any serious artillery fire. However, of course for the targeting of point or dot targets where you need precision targeting, they can of course be used. Because they are high precision weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, I don't understand why you're expanding on your answer now and explaining all this to us. Let me remind you of your order of the 11th of November, 1991, and it is Exhibit P118, P118 is the number of this document. And under item 4, for example, point 4, it says: "TOC Prevlaka," and says from 8.00 to 8.30 hours on the 12th of November with a Howitzer of 122 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we have the document in front of us, and may the witness have the document in front of him, if it's going to be referred to in such detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P118 is the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Under point 4, a combat order is being issued to the TOC Prevlaka. And it says that from 0800 to 0830 hours on the 12th of November, 1991, with a 122-millimetre Howitzer and a 120-millimetre mortar platoon, support for the 3rd -- gun support attack of the 3rd Light Infantry Brigade Komolac from -- support for 3rd Light Infantry Brigades attack by carrying out strikes on the K31 Komolac sector from 0800 hours to 0830 hours, as on the 12th of November, 1991, with 122-millimetre Howitzer and 120-millimetre mortar platoon. From 0800 hours to 0900 hours on the 12th of November, 1991, with a 130 gun support attack of the 3rd Light Infantry Brigade, inflicting strikes on the Cakovica village sector. From 0830 to 0900 hours on the 12th of November, 1991, strikes on such with 122-millimetre Howitzer, 120-millimetre mortar platoon. Did you issue that order to the TOC?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's not being challenged at all. The only mistake is that this V ^ isn't a mortar platoon. It is an artillery piece of 120 millimetre. It is not a mortar platoon as it says here, it is just a weapon. Because we have 122, 120, and one 130-millimetre artillery piece.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, we're not going into that kind of detail now. What I want to know is this: Did you issue a combat order of this type to the unit that was entitled TOC, and according to this order we saw when it was expected to be deployed and how.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's no denying that. Of course it's quite obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: If there's no denying it, I'm asking you is the TOC within the 9th VPS? It's missing in the diagram, so could you please enter it into the diagram. Or are you stating up to the very end that it's not within your units?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said how come this happened, and I said that it was never my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was it subordinated to you at that time, at that moment? You also entered the 3rd LPBR, which was also never a unit of yours. Right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a unit that was brought in and subordinated to me, whereas the TOC is not a combat unit and it is subordinated to the military technical institute. It was used -- it, rather, only used these experimental weapons for point objectives in Vitaljina and Molunat.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Please do not expand. I'm just asking you whether on the 6th of December, the TOC was also within the 9th VPS with their artillery pieces, no matter how many there were?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what I said and that is what is written on this diagram.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me whether the 130th Engineering Battalion is also among your units?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you enter it as well? Did you write it down?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said that I had other units that I can write in. If they are significance, I'll do it right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you just read these new units out to us, the ones that are written next to TOC?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says the 130th Engineering Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 9th Battalion of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 9th Battalion of signals. The 9th Company of OSOJ, the coastal service for observation and reporting.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I'd just like to ask you something. The first box, where it says "BORB," that 204th ORD?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that time, it was not the 204th ORD. It became a divizion only when the battery of land-to-sea rockets were mobilised from other sectors. And I had only one battery initially.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, in your orders, was there any reference to the 400 -- 204th ORD or the way you wrote it down in this diagram now?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see the relevance of that. I'm telling you about what the organisation was and the situation that I found there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you, Mr. Jokic, how many soldiers there were and whether they had breakfast. I am asking you whether in your orders there is mention of the 204th ORD, or the designation that you put in this box now. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember such details.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to ask you to put the date of the 6th of December on this piece of paper and to sign it on the front page, please.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to ask for this document to be identified as a Defence exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You tendered the document; it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will be marked D46.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the usher to place document P101 in front of the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Is this your order dated the 20th of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 1, does it say that according to the decision of the commander of the 2nd Operational Group dated the 19th of November, 1991, the 472nd Motorised Brigade without the 3rd Motorised Battalion will be out of the 9th VPS and will function under the command of the 2nd Operational Group, specifically the 2nd Corps within which it will operate. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. But I have an explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Please, I don't need any explanations. I just want us to state facts.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... is answering. We'd ask that he be permitted to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No, he's not wanting to answer, he wants to explain an answer. So we'll leave that to re-examination, if necessary. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Until when was the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade within your units?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, until the 31st of December, which is what is relevant here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was that the deadline by which it remained within the 9th VPS?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the deadline was. I asked for it to be taken out immediately after the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you remember approximately until when it remained within your units? Was it during -- was it within your units during the course of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the beginning, but I don't know when it was replaced, when the negotiations started or whether it went on leave. I don't know. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was it, say, there on the 5th of February, 1992, within your units? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It probably was, probably so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: What about the month of March 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know. I know that Kovacevic, Captain Kovacevic, disappeared that time, in February. But I don't know whether the battalion remained.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you remember at all until when you commanded the 3rd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said that it was there in 1992, but I don't know when it was replaced. For a long time, it was out of action; it was on leave. And it probably stayed on longer, but I don't know how long exactly in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: When my learned friend of the Prosecution asked you during the examination-in-chief, you said that bearing in mind the strength of the 472nd Motorised Brigade and constant provocations that you proposed to General Strugar that this brigade be taken out of the area surrounding Dubrovnik and that he accepted that. Can that be seen from this order?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. On the 2nd of November or even before that I --

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Just briefly, please. Is it correct or not?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You've already explained.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. I asked for this brigade to be taken out as far back as the 25th of October and when he subordinated to me. And he -- and I explained why I asked for that. He said we are going to resolve that within a couple of days. And then on the 2nd of November he really issued orders for this brigade to be taken out of the 9th Sector, or rather, out of the blockade of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Why are you constantly running away from the 472nd Brigade? And it is a unit that belonged originally to the 9th VPS. Are you ashamed of the fact that that brigade was within the 9th VPS?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, this is the right question, truly. Before, I used to be proud of that brigade. However, from the 1st of October until the 25th of October, in this so-called Dubrovnik operation, this brigade in the blockade of Dubrovnik took action that was self-defeating. It did not achieve any success. It had an excessive use of artillery. By shelling neighbourhoods in Rijeka Dubrovacka, and all settlements from Cavtat, Mlini to Zupa Dubrovacka. There were many provocations and action was taken even when cease-fire -- when a cease-fire was ordered. There were too many casualties, dead and wounded, due to a lack of discipline, lack of fire discipline, poor reconnaissance, poor command, and so on. As a matter of fact, three soldiers from the 2nd Tactical Group were wounded by their artillery in the Mlini/Zvekovica area. In appreciation of the potential danger for Dubrovnik, if this unit in the area surrounding the town was inactive, I was truly against having that unit join my units. At all costs, I asked General Strugar not to accept it. As a matter of fact, I did not even go to its command post ever - and that was Ljubovo and Cerovac - which was my duty as commander. Those are the reasons, to put it quite sincerely. That is why I did not want that unit to remain around town and within my units.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, we've just heard something that I don't want to repeat later on. But if you have anything else to add linked to the 472nd Brigade, tell us now so that we don't have to go into additional explanations later on.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I did. General Strugar accepted my proposal, and on the 2nd of November he ordered that withdrawal with the date of the 6th of November, effective of that date. On the 6th of November, only the 4th battalion was pulled out and sent to Slano. And instead of it, I left the mixed detachment of the Territorial Defence. The 3rd Battalion was already pulled out and was on leave in Trebinje from the 25th of October, in fact, which means that it wasn't within the composition of the brigade. And I didn't come across it or see it. And on the 6th of November, General Strugar really did order the withdrawal of the brigade. However, it did not withdraw. Two battalions across the Dubrovacka Rijeka, the 1st and 2nd, stayed on. They remained in their positions. The units which were supposed to replace the brigade arrived in their areas of combat deployment ready to replace the previous ones, and they were the 3rd Light Brigade, the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade, the detachment of the Territorial Defence of Trebinje, and the battalion of the Territorial Defence of Trebinje. However, the takeover of duty did not take place, and at that time I myself on the 6th of December [as interpreted] find myself with double units, or rather, the ones I enumerated and the 472nd Brigade minus two battalions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. Correction in the transcript. It should say 6th of November not 6th of December on line 10, page 14.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right. The 6th of November. On the 7th of November, the chief of the General Staff ordered that a total blockade should be effected of the ports in the Dubrovnik region because of the problems of the blocked garrisons in Croatia. However, the order for that same day with respect to the 472nd Brigade from the 2nd Operational Group read as follows: "Continue with the replacement of the units of the brigade." On the 8th of November, the attacks started in order to take control of the Bosanka fortress and the Dubrovacka Rijeka. And for that day, what it said was: "Continue with the replacement of the brigade," as it did for the forthcoming days, not to have to repeat what I've already said. On the 9th -- between the 9th and 10th, the 3rd Battalion was introduced of that brigade, coming back from leave. Thank you for giving me the time to go into that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I hope you've had a chance to explain what you wanted to now.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: That you had sufficient time. Just tell me now, please, under item 1 of this order, is there any mention made of the order for the 2nd Operational Group by which that brigade -- that group is drawn out of the VPS and attached to the 2nd Corps, just briefly, please, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And when you say that the 3rd Battalion on the 25th of October was pulled out and no longer remained within the composition of the brigade, do you mean to say by that that at that time it was not at its positions but that the people were already on leave, but of course formationally speaking, they were still within the composition of that brigade, weren't they? They would be right, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The unit wasn't at its positions, but of course it was within the composition of the brigade. It was just not at its positions [Realtime transcript read in error "It was just at its positions"].

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You mentioned that you never went to the command post of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there's a problem with the interpretation. The witness said it was not at its positions, but of course it was within the composition of the brigade. That is line 15. Lines 22 and 23 do not reflect that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You said, if I understood you correctly, that while the brigade was under your command, that you did not ever tour the command post of that brigade. Is that right? You didn't go there. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you, in that way, wish to show them, to demonstrate your anger by ignoring them, or was it something else entirely?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there's a grain of truth in that. That was more or less what it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Isn't it a little strange and unusual for a commander, corps commander, which would be what the 9th VPS was, is angry at a brigade within its composition and does not contact or tour it at all, visit it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've already explained that it was under me for just a few days, just two of its battalions. And its withdrawal was expected imminently. Whereas this situation, this withdrawal, went on from one day to the next. It was prolonged. And bearing that in mind -- rather, the fact that the unit both did come under me and didn't come under me and was there and was not there, it was in the process of leaving, that was the reason for this attitude that I took, except for what I've already explained.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was there a deficiency in your commanding there then, the way you exerted your command?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can put it that way if you like. It depends on your assessment and appraisal.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Well, when I asked you this, I had in mind first and foremost the rules and regulations of the JNA, its doctrine, JNA doctrine, and specifications, the doctrine of control and command. Unless I'm wrong, it doesn't state anywhere that the superior commander can be angry with a subordinate unit and not visit it. I think I'm right in saying that, in disregarding it at all.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, rules and regulations in the army did not regulate life and relationships. And the question of anger is quite unsuited, but I do agree with respect to collecting the unit, yes. However, let me say again that we are dealing with a space of five days or rather seven days. This went on for seven days, this subordination and detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was it regulated in the rules of control and command, this type of situation, that a superior commander cannot be angry and avoid and neglect his unit?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we pursue this, then the command of the 2nd Defence Group came to see me just once when he took over his duties in Kumbor, for example in 1991. And in Kupari, he came by once.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Defence group, operational group, is unclear what the original B/C/S --

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Operative, operational --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... in line 19, page 17.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Regardless of the fact that you mentioned General Strugar, as far as I understood your examination-in-chief, you said you had a very proper relationship with him.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: However, a moment ago you explained to us specifically your animosity towards the 472nd Brigade while it was within your composition. So all I was asking you was if you recognise that these were deficiencies or weaknesses or faults. Do you agree that pursuant to the rules of control and command, this kind of situation is not provided for and conduct of that kind is not in the rules and regulations?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I be allowed to explain at greater length, as you keep insisting upon this point?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I think the answer is simple. Just give us a yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you can't give a yes or no answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Then explain.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the brigade commander just one, and the man, he was Colonel Obrad Vicic. He was not in command of the brigade, and everybody knows that, including the command of the 2nd Operational Group. Although in formal official terms, he was the group's commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you tour units of that brigade, regardless of whether Obrad Vicic was present or not? The brigade was composed of four battalions, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it was within my composition, under me, I did visit its units. And of course the chief of staff of that brigade, who was in command of it, pursuant to my order, came when the brigade was operational and effective.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't completed my answer, but if you don't want to hear it, never mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: The Prosecution will ask you about that, that second portion, because we've spent quite a lot of time on it already. Now, you also said that upon arrival at the Dubrovnik theatre of operations on the 17th of November, you saw a lot of men belonging to the 2nd Tactical Group in a small area. And as there was no military necessity for so many men to be present, you proposed to General Strugar that from the 2nd Tactical Group forces be withdrawn, that is to say the 1st Partizan Brigade of the Territorial Defence, and I'm asking you now whether that proposal was taken up or not, was it adopted? Was that brigade indeed withdrawn?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The proposal was adopted several days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that afterwards the 2nd Tactical Group was disbanded soon afterwards?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not immediately afterwards. It was disbanded on the 21st of October. And they spent too much time, the two brigades and two battalions, acted in this very narrow region and resorted to artillery fire and other means. But General Strugar did withdraw the brigade, one brigade, and then disbanded it following the request, and when he saw this to be a military and tactical necessity.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: For the transcript, it says the 17th of November. So can we clear that point up, this withdrawal of that brigade from the 2nd Tactical Group and the disbanding of the tactical group itself. Did this take place in October 1991?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Now, you also said that General Strugar otherwise asked a proposal from his subordinate commanders on the best deployment of the unit, on the basis of which he took his decision on resubordination and attachment. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you happen to remember whether you perhaps made a proposal along those lines with respect to the deployment of the TO units?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when it comes to Territorial Defence units, there were quite a lot of problems because they were fragmented, the territorial companies from the different municipalities. I know that General Djurickovic was appointed, the chief of staff of the Territorial Defence of Montenegro as coordinator for the deployment and use of those units and the 9th Sector. A little before my arrival or as I was arriving, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, may I interrupt you. The substance of my question was this: As you made these proposals, did you make similar proposals when it came to the TO units? Let me remind you, you spoke about the formation of a mixed detachment of the Territorial Defence, for instance. So that's what I mean. Did you propose things of that type to the command of the 2nd OG?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. And I've said so already.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to ask you to take a look at the order and to tell me under item 3 -- I apologise, item 4. The platoon, ZIS platoon of the 472nd Motorised Brigade, was it pulled out of the 472nd Brigade and became a part of the 2nd Partizan Motorised Brigade [as interpreted], which I think is discussed in item 3 and explained further under item 4?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. That's precisely what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, page 21, line 5, mentions the 2nd Partizan Motorised Brigade, whereas it should be the 5th one, the 5th Partizan Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me, this ZIS platoon, what weapons did it have and what -- how many?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were 76-millimetre anti-armour weapons used for anti-armour combat, and I think that a platoon has two pieces. And here it says that their task was to prevent naval traffic in the Kolocep canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In coordination with whom?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Please read under item 3, second sentence. It says here --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, you're right. The 3rd Light Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Item 3, it says as follows in the second sentence --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: "During the day, except a platoon of ZIS in the 472nd Motorised Brigade into the company at Zaton and select a position for it so that it efficiently cuts off maritime traffic in coordination with the 40-millimetre TV of the 204th ORD."

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: So you see that it mentions the 204th ORD, which is the rocket artillery battalion, and not as you told us OAD, which is the coastal rocket artillery battalion?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did not have the divizion, the artillery battalion. The fact that this is mentioned here just means that we did not have a full strength as we should have had.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, I think that you are avoiding answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Well, when I asked you what the unit is called, then you should really give me the name of the unit as it was known within the formation and not give me the number of soldiers that that unit had. I think that the matter is quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That unit had one battery. This is why I wrote that down, as far as I know. And I don't know if that means anything to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you ever propose that a name of that unit be changed, because it only had one battery, as you state?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Following the evacuation, this unit received -- was given, was assigned, another two batteries after the evacuation of Sibenik and Pula sectors.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: But it remained known as the artillery battalion?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what does the TV 40 millimetre stand for?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a tank platoon of 40 millimetres -- sorry, gun platoon of 40 millimetres. And it is used to provide support -- air support.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, page 22, line 24, says "tank platoon" and it should be "gun platoon."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That has already been corrected. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at item 5 of the order. Could you please explain what these abbreviations stand for.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anti-armour coastal battery within the 107th OAD of the coastal artillery battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does item 5 state that these two units should take over weapons and ammunition from TOC, as is stated here?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown Exhibit P102. I don't know whether there is a translation, English translation, for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We have one.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, this is a document issued by the command of the 2nd Operational Group dated the 2nd -- 5th of February, 1992. And it was sent to the federal secretariat for national defence, the General Staff of the armed forces of SFRY, the first administration, and it speaks about the composition in this system of the units of JNA, Territorial Defence, and volunteer units. So they are replying to the telegram sent to them by the secretariat and the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Under item 3 -- no, item 5. It says here: "VPS Boka." And then under that we have the JNA units; they are listed. Please tell me whether under the JNA units on the 5th of February within your composition there was the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. And the 1st Battalion of the 5th Brigade, which is a mistake, which is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Could you please take a look at item 3 on -- it starts on page 1 and then it lists the 13th Corps and goes on to list further details on the following page. And then it says the command and it lists the units within that command. Is the most frequently used term "not filled" or "not ready for combat"?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that this corps was established in late 1991; that's when they started establishing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell me, under item 2 we have subitems A and B on page 1. And then below that it says that all units are under the command of the 2nd Corps. The volunteer units have been established by the command of the 2nd Corps and the command of the military district of Titograd, pursuant to the order of the 3rd administration of the General Staff. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Also under item 5, C, which is on the last page at the top, it lists there the 3rd Light Infantry Brigade and it goes on to say that it was established pursuant to the order of the command of the 2nd Corps and approval or consent of the 3rd administration of the General Staff of the armed forces and that there had been no pressure exerted by political parties. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. And this unit was placed under my command.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Does this reflect the problems in establishing full strength of the JNA units -- in achieving full strength of the JNA units and establishing them?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And that the 3rd administration of the General Staff had to intervene in order to achieve this?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a significant problem with achieving full strength of units. There were many large units in a small area. The mobilisational standards had changed concerning the filling of the units, these standards that applied in peacetime.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you spoke about the lack of discipline, you said that the command of the 2nd OG used to order daily that strict measures be taken in order to prevent that, however that it was difficult to prevent and put an end to this type of behaviour because the circumstances were such that they were not favourable for command. Could you please explain that a bit more. What was meant under this term "circumstances," the circumstances as they existed?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this phrase "circumstances" in my mind means as follows: The state of war had not been declared, however the units were engaged in combat and suffered losses. The general goals and objectives were not clear, military goals and objectives in the conduct of operations. And for days at a time, we didn't know whether we should advance or whether we should remain in place. The soldiers were not motivated for action. Particularly when the blockade of Dubrovnik started, in the circumstances where there was no intention to take the city itself, and in a situation where the residents of Dubrovnik did not accept the order to surrender weapons and to demilitarise the town. Political parties had influence, especially over the reserve forces and a very negative influence it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You mean political parties?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I said political parties; they had very negative influence over the reserve forces. And the media, which was engaged in warmongering, had a most negative influence of all. They incited people to go to war. And the policies taken by the state worked towards achieving a peaceful solution, but only formally. Whereas, in reality they did not accept a compromise and a peaceful resolution of the crisis.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that a convenient time, Mr. Rodic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will have the first morning break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, before the break you explained to us what the situation was like, and you said that it was not in favour of the command as far as military discipline was concerned. However, beforehand you said anything thing, that command efforts in resolving problems of discipline yielded partial results only, because the system-related causes had not been eradicated. When you say system-related causes, I believe that you mean the overall situation you referred to just now. I'm asking you now whether these system-related causes also include --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. I think it would be appropriate to ask what he meant by that, not to speculate as to what he meant by that and then take the question from there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, it could be shorter and more simple and more useful to us to get the witness's view of what he means, rather than you explore all possible possibilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tried to keep it as short as possible, but I'm going to ask the witness then what he meant by these system-related causes, that they had not been eradicated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I meant in respect of resolving problems of a lack of discipline amongst the personnel, amongst the military, both soldiers and officers. The military courts did not exist attached to armies, or rather, they had not been evacuated into this area or established in this area. The military criminal court did not function. So disciplinary infractions, violations, and crimes were sanctioned only later, sometime toward the end of November or beginning of December or the very beginning of December. Since a state of war had not been declared, not a single commander felt accountable as a commander in a particular zone, not only for combat operations, but everything else that was taking place within that area, as is regulated by wartime military regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just an addition to the transcript, if you allow. Page 27, line 18, it only says "military courts," but it is the military discipline courts that the witness referred to. And then later, he explains the military criminal courts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, establishing units in haste, is that one of these system-related causes?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, as far as command and control is concerned, in haste. And also, commands that are temporarily resubordinated. They were not stabilised; they were not trained. Officers barely knew each other. And all of this had a negative effect on command and control.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: All these circumstances that you referred to in response to my first question and also these system-related causes that you mentioned just now, did the 2nd Operational Group have any influence over all of that, or were these causes and conditions there independently of the 2nd Operational Group?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of the 2nd Operational Group, of course, like all other commands, could not change the objective circumstances involved, especially not over such a short span of time, three months. A lot more time was needed for the military's fear and for command and control, for the situation to be improved from that point of view.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the usher to show the witness P107, which is in tab 8 of the Prosecution exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, this is an order of the command of the 9th Military Naval Sector addressed to all subordinate commands. It pertains to your order for improving discipline. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 1, does it say that "While touring the units, the organs of the VPS discovered that orders were not getting through to those ultimately carrying them out. There have been a host of unlawfully acts, incorrect actions, and behaviour of individuals and units, willfulness, lack of discipline, abuse, and failure to follow and carry out orders." And then in order to improve general disorder and discipline, did you issue this order?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the objective, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that through this order you address your subordinate units and give them tasks and instructions, on the basis of which all weaknesses that were noted during this tour should be eliminated?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was this the only order, or did you have other orders during this period, October to December 1991, in which you insisted on the respect of order and discipline?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. There were many orders, an inflation of orders. A seminar was held on overall problems that infringe upon the morale and combat-readiness of the troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you have any return information that these orders of yours went down to the lowest-ranking units that were subordinated to you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These orders mainly went down to the basic units as well; however, the greatest problems were not in the navy units. In the units that were manned primarily by military conscripts who were serving their -- who were doing their military service at the time. The greatest problem were -- problems were in the units of the 472nd Brigade and the 3rd Light Brigade. And in part, among the territorial units, I mean the territorial companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: This more negative situation that you refer to, does it primarily pertain to units that were manned by reservists, where there were not regular soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the usher to give the witness P109, which is in tab 9(A).

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: This is on order of your command dated the 1st of November, 1991, for governing the life and work of units in combat, and it was sent to all subordinate units. Right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was this order written after the representatives of the command of the 2nd Operational Group toured the units and presented their observations -- sorry, I withdraw this question. The order of the 1st of November, 1991, that is to say this order, you in this order caution your units to fully observe the orders of the command of the 2nd Operational Group, especially confidential order number 343-1 of the 18th of October, 1991, and confidential number 547-1 of the 30th of October, 1991. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, except that this focuses on combat safety, although the other weaknesses were still there. Because the reason why this was mentioned was a diversion in Slavonia, where there were many casualties involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Does command also bear in mind the orders of the 2nd Operational Group, and through this particular order did you ask your subordinates to eliminate these weaknesses more efficiently and faster?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: On page 2, towards the end, it says what all your units were, rather, all of those that this order was sent to.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the usher to give the witness P110, which is in tab 10 of the Prosecution exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: On the 4th of December, you as commander approved of a plan of measures and activities aimed at developing and maintaining order and discipline and morale of units in the next period. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, was this also in line with the orders issued by the superior command in order to eliminate the problems that we have already discussed?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, except that what is listed here is this entire spectrum of measures and activities that effect morale and combat-readiness of units.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that problems were analysed and that attempts were made to deal with them in detail and to improve the situation in terms of the life and work of the troops involved?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher help us, please, and provide the witness with P112, an exhibit in tab 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me, please, whether this order issued after the instructions came from the federal secretariat of national defence and the order of that same body, the secretariat, with respect to the problems with respect to the seized property on the battlefront, whether this is the order.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This order was issued based on an initial order and instructions from the federal secretariat of national defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Take a look at point 6 of that order. Item 6, does it indicate that the superior -- that the officers and organs of the military units issued permits for taking over confiscated and seized supplies and materiel?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And what is being ordered under point 6 in actual fact, what measures are to be taken?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this item, documents are called for, notarised copies or photocopies with respect to the issuance of supplies, that is to say to the organs of civilian administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Is this being ordered so that records could be kept in one place of what was issued, a united set of records?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. For there to be complete records of supplies issued and also to collect those supplies in a central place, a collection centre in other words.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: On several occasions you mentioned the unpleasantness that you had in the press with respect to bringing your name in context with the seized supplies. Your name was mentioned in that regard. Now, tell me, please, did you play any part in that, in assisting Banja Vrujica and Mionica to gain equipment and the agricultural concern in Lajkovac [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to give an explanation here about that. Everything that appeared in the press, and several articles appeared in the papers, papers which wanted to shift the guilt for all the looting that went on and to take the blame away from certain individuals and put the blame on me. I can explain that if you want to later on. And as for this particular case, the facts are these: In order to pull out meat products from the Pula sector, my command did not have refrigerators. And at my request, this agricultural concern sent a new refrigerator with -- manned with five individuals. Now, when these supplies were evacuated, the vessel which carried this refrigerator around the waters of the island of Vis sunk, but luckily everybody on board was saved. Several days later, the director turned up, together with the president of the municipality or mayor, and asked how we were going to make up for this refrigerator and send him one back. I told him that I couldn't do that and that he should contact the military authorities who drew up the contract in the first place, with the foreign vessel which was intentionally sunk, that he should be remunerated and the losses and damages paid for, that he should contact the insurance company. And at the same time, the president of the municipality made a request asking for assistance to refugees from Croatia who were presently located in Banja Vrujica, a spa. And the administration for civilian affairs had already been established by that time. Colonel Pipovic was in command and it was directly subordinated to General Strugar, so that I had nothing to do with that there, with the property that they disposed of. I sent them -- I told them to contact Colonel Pipovic and ordered Captain Zec to deal with the situation, because I didn't wish to get involved because they were from my own municipality. So they went there, took over the supplies and resources they were lacking in this refugee centre. Mostly they were -- it was furniture which they were allotted from the military warehouses at Prevlaka. Of course all those items were paid for according to tariffs determined by the administration for civilian affairs. And the security organs who investigated this particular case, the state security and military organs, did so because I was the target ever since I was in government. So they investigated the -- this case very thoroughly. And then they went to Banja to see, Banja Vrujica, whether the inventory had been registered and recorded, whether all the goods had been paid for. They compared the lists they found with the ones that they had at the Sutorina collection centre. And since there were no discrepancies or any grounds for further investigation, the matter died a natural death and wasn't interesting anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: So all the documentation was regularly recorded?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: However, what the press wrote about and what was on television, I was attacked twice -- or rather, once but not a second -- I was attacked twice, but others weren't. But we'll come to that perhaps later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask the usher to provide the witness with Prosecution exhibit 113 from tab 13 now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: This is an order which follows on from the problems dealt with by the previous order, the one we've just been discussing. This is an addition to this order. Would that be correct? An addendum, in fact?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I should now like to ask you to explain point 3 of this order of yours at greater length, please.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, what this says is the following: After logging and recording all these supplies in the assembly or collection centre, that the -- this should be sold, supplies should be sold, and the funds gained thereby provided -- and to be used as assistance to the family of fallen soldiers and the erection of monuments to their memory. I think that this has been copied from the order issued by the command of the 2nd Operational Group, because I didn't have the right to order anything to this assembly or collection centre or Colonel Pipovic, who headed the centre. With his arrival in the operation zone, I and all the other commanders were relieved of all responsibility for dealing with problems of goods that had been seized and confiscated.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, all the activities with respect to keeping logbooks and records of the various goods and supplies and ultimately the selling of supplies in these collection or assembly centres, were these regulated by instructions and regulations issued in the federal secretariat for national defence?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Formally speaking, that was how it was; however, in practice things were quite different.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher assist us now again, please, and show the witness exhibit 45, to be found in tab 14.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: This is an order by the federal secretariat of national defence, the General Staff of the armed forces of the SFRY, the 1st administration operative centre. It is dated the 20-something of September, 29th of September, 1991, determining how regular combat reports are to be sent in. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Could you clarify point 1 of this order, please.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What it states is that the commands of the military districts are to submit regular combat reports on the basis of the reports by their subordinate brigades, et cetera, of the corps from third levels down up to individual battalion, divisions, et cetera. And this should be sent in --

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. I'm interested in point 1 and what it says in the first sentence. It says: "From three levels down for all units and detached formations." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Now, does this refer to the fact that the commands of the military districts should submit regular combat reports on the basis of regular combat reports sent by the brigades and corps, depending on the units under their -- within their formation.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Now, does this mean, by the same token, that when it says "three levels down," that it explains which units are duty-bound to compile regular combat reports? Is that what it means?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. An independent battalion is the lowest unit, or rather, it is a formational regiment. And a detached formation or independent battalion is that third level down, which has this obligation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the question, the microphone was off.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Is it true that this 2nd Operative Group received regular combat reports from the 9th VPS, the 2nd Corps, and the 37th Corps, based on the first table drawn by you when --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And to clarify this further, regular combat reports of the 9th VPS were compiled by you based on regular combat reports of the subordinate units down to the level of battalion. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Independent battalion; brigade, independent battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Let's just clarify this then. If the independent battalion under the command -- is under the command of the 9th VPS, then it doesn't have this obligation to send regular combat reports to the command of the 2nd Operative Group. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. No, no regular combat reports, just interim ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please take a look at the last paragraph of this order, where it says that: "The operative duty team of the federal secretariat for national defence is to keep the operative logbook and the work map." Please tell us whether this means that the operative duty team is to keep this logbook and the work map for the General Staff and the federal secretariat precisely pursuant to these combat reports that it receives from the listed units.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Does this mean, then, that the military leadership is aware of the situation on the ground where the subordinated units are?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In principle, yes. The 1st administration is in charge of the entire situation in the JNA, and that means that the General Staff should have all this information in their operative logbook and the work map.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Please tell us whether by analysing this situation, the federal secretariat of national defence and the General Staff go on to issue further orders and goals to their subordinate commands.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the procedure, the prescribed procedure, for decision making and deployment of forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown Exhibit P114, which is to be found in tab 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: At first glance, what is your first impression? Does this document look like a typical document of the federal secretariat for national defence?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bearing in mind that this was drafted by the administration for morale guidance, I would say yes, this looks like a document drafted by them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And how come that the document of the administration for morale guidance of the federal secretariat for national defence is signed by the chief of the General Staff, General Blagoje Adzic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is strange, too. Normally he wouldn't sign this. He would sign this on behalf of the federal secretary, because this is not within his scope of authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me who was the head of the administration for morale guidance? What general held that office at the time?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, it was Lieutenant General Marko Njegovanovic. He held that office at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was he authorised to sign a document of this nature?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was. And he used to send to us information on negotiations led concerning the Yugoslav crisis. We received two or three such reports from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Please tell us whether General Adzic, as the chief of the General Staff, also had an assistant for the matters of this nature.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he had an assistant. Why would he have one? Well, perhaps somebody was in charge of this, but this field this -- these matters of -- for morale guidance were normally under the jurisdiction of the federal secretariat for national defence and not the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you, within the 9th VPS, have an assistant for morale guidance or MPV, as it was called?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, naturally. However, we're dealing here with the supreme command which was established at the time. I don't know exactly what the organisational system of the supreme command was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: But it would have been logical to have an assistant chief of the General Staff within the General Staff in charge of these matters?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you precisely. It's possible in the peacetime, yes. However, as I said, the supreme command was established at the time and I don't know how it was organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Very well. I would like to ask you to take a look at paragraph 5 on the first page, which begins with the sentence: "In keeping the constitutional obligations."

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: What does this paragraph explain?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It discusses constitutional obligations of the Yugoslav People's Army with respect to the protection of the Serbian people in Croatia. And then it also mentions the imprisoned members of the JNA, or captured members of the JNA, and their families and the prevention of the ethnic cleansing of the territory of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And the blockade of barracks?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: What about paragraph 7? "In order to have this task achieved"?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In order to successfully achieve that goal, the blockade around the barracks in Croatia must be lifted as soon as possible, and units must be pulled out of them and moved to new locations. This would, besides saving human lives, also strengthen forces for the army's main task.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Could you please clarify the second and the third paragraph on the following page. It says: "That is why the presidency of the SFRY" --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, "the presidency of the SFRY has taken a clear position that the withdrawal of the JNA units from Croatian territories inhabited by Serbs would be unacceptable. Because that would expose them to physical elimination. In accordance with the above, the presidency has decided that until a political resolution is achieved, a political resolution of the Yugoslav crisis, the military forces are to stay where they are. Once political solutions are adopted, the JNA will act in accordance with the political decisions and agreements that are achieved."

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Now, let us look at another paragraph -- or rather, is it true that it states here that Veljko -- General Veljko Kadijevic sent a similar reply to the Dutch minister Van Den Broek who at the time was chairman of the European Community -- president of the European Community?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: All right. In paragraph 6 could you please tell us what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "All our men should be aware of the importance of this task so that they can show understanding and have patience. It is obvious that no surprises should be allowed in these circumstances. Every provocation should be met with decisiveness and without any hesitation."

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: This last sentence that you have just read, is it clear and specific enough?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so. "Every provocation [Realtime transcript read in error "decision"] should be met with decisiveness and without any hesitation."

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell us, were you aware of these positions that are stated in this letter?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, page 42, line 15. It says here: "Every decision," where in fact it should be "every provocation." This is what the witness stated: "Every provocation should be met with decisiveness and without any hesitation."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I add something to this issue involving provocations. It might be useful. Your Honours, we had problems with provocations, coming both from our side and from the Croatian side, due to lack of discipline among units on both sides, among volunteers, and the extreme elements and so on. The orders were to deter and prevent these provocations, mostly from our side. Whereas, when it came to provocations from their side, the orders were initially to respond to them. And after that, the orders were not to respond to them unless these provocations were potentially dangerous and could lead to losses. Following that, there was an order not to respond. And if there was a response, to ensure that it was a destructive type of response. We had an order that specified that a vital element of a military facility on the opposite side, the Croatian side, is to be destroyed. And then towards the end, sometime in December just before the negotiations on cease-fire and peace, we received an order from the chief of the General Staff -- or rather, the order was relayed to me verbally not to respond to firing, to keep our units under control, to sign a cease-fire -- a truce, and to be flexible.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Were you acquainted with all these orders? Were you familiar with them?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: All right. Since you also said that you were aware of this document sent by the administration for morale guidance, please tell us whether this administration explained the situation in which the country was and the JNA was clearly enough. Did it also explain the tasks that the JNA was to accomplish?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There's no denying that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can we just finish this. In this document it says that --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honours, the witness was in the process of giving a response and he was cut off. There's been a number of occasions where the Prosecution was asked not to cut off the witness, so we minded it. And I would ask that the witness be allowed to finish his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I hadn't detected any unreasonable attempt to deal with the evidence. Was there something, Admiral, you were concerned to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes. I don't know how important it is now, but this is what I wish to say: This is a political document. It explains the situation regarding the crisis and action taken by units and so on and so forth. However, the problem of provocations and responding to provocations is not resolved by organs for political affairs. That is for the command structures to deal with. And it has to do with clear orders that are to be given by superior commanders, superior officers. That's the only thing I wish to add.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And tell us then General Blagoje Adzic, the person who signed this document as it says at the end of this document, is he this command structure?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
